evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 10.27 mg/L (46.0h) to 1.69 mg/L (46.2h) and stays 1.0-1.7 mg/L through 52.0h — below the 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving P assay at t=48h = 2.57 g/L vs source-1 3.06, source-2 3.02, source-3 2.98 g/L at the same age
DO2 at decision time (52.0h) = 1.13 mg/L, lowest reading in the record
Source batches under KEEP never dropped below ~7.4 mg/L, confirming the receiving vessel has a distinct, worse oxygen balance
Allowed action bounds: strong_feed_reduction = feed 0.6, air 1.15; combined = feed 0.8, air 1.15; keep = 1.0/1.0
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation is in a sustained, worsening oxygen-constraint violation: DO2 fell abruptly at 46.2h from ~10 mg/L to ~1.1-1.7 mg/L and remains ~1.13 mg/L at the 52h decision time, well below the 2.0 mg/L minimum. The 15% aeration increase alone (increase_air) is unlikely to close a gap of this magnitude given the ~9 mg/L deficit relative to pre-crash levels, and KEEP guarantees continued violation. A feed reduction lowers oxygen uptake demand directly and, unlike stop, retains the accumulated product mass and keeps production counting. I select the bounded strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) because it combines the largest demand reduction with the maximum allowed aeration increase, giving the best margin to restore DO2 above 2.0 mg/L. The milder combined (x0.8, x1.15) risks leaving DO2 near or below the constraint if uptake is strongly feed-driven; stop is rejected outright since it produces zero counted production and discards in-progress product. The 4h lag on an extra assay (returning ~56h under KEEP) would leave the violation unaddressed for another cycle, so I act now rather than request the assay.
submission.uncertainty: The hidden relationship between feed rate, aeration, and OUR is unknown, so I cannot confirm that even x0.6 feed plus x1.15 air restores DO2 above 2.0 mg/L; if uptake is substrate-saturated, the feed cut may be insufficient and only stop would resolve the violation (at zero production). Product trajectory shows a lag/plateau (sources peaked ~8.3 g/L then declined to ~6.4-7.9 g/L by 96h), so even after re-oxygenation, final titer and total counted mass remain uncertain. Aeration headroom above 1.15x is also not established; if the air constraint binds, the expected DO recovery is overstated.

evidence: Receiving DO2 observations t=46.2-52.0 h: sustained 1.0-1.7 mg/L, below minimum_do_mg_l=2.0
Source batches never fell below ~7.4 mg/L DO2 at matched times, indicating receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit
Delayed P assay: receiving 2.57 g/L at 48 h vs source 2.98-3.06 g/L

Forward model comparison: strong_feed_reduction gives lowest below-limit hours (10.4), lowest oxygen deficit (8.76 mg·h/L), highest min DO (0.81 mg/L), highest product mass (128.74 kg) among all actions
Model estimated transfer multiplier 0.40, indicating source-calibrated model substantially overpredicts receiving DO capacity; relative action ranking still favors the 0.6-feed/1.15-air intervention
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 collapsed at ~46.2 h to 1.0-1.7 mg/L, well below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen operating minimum, and has stayed there for ~6 h — an active constraint violation that KEEP would perpetuate. Source batches never dropped below ~7 mg/L at comparable times, confirming a receiving-specific oxygen-transfer deficit (model-estimated transfer multiplier ~0.40). Of the bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (feed ×0.6, air ×1.15) is the best trade-off: the forward model shows it yields the fewest below-limit hours (10.4 vs 13-17.4 for other actions), the smallest post-decision oxygen deficit (8.76 vs 11.4-13.3 mg·h/L), the highest minimum DO, and the highest retained product mass (~128.74 kg). Reduce_feed or increase_air alone address only one side of the oxygen balance; the strong combined action attacks both oxygen demand and supply. A stop is rejected because it zeroes counted production. Although the source-calibrated model is imperfect and predicts no action fully restores DO ≥ 2.0 mg/L, strong_feed_reduction dominates the relative ranking on every oxygen and mass metric.
submission.uncertainty: The physical forward model is calibrated on source batches with an estimated transfer multiplier of 0.40, so its absolute DO predictions likely underestimate the receiving vessel; its predicted absolute infeasibility under all actions should not be taken as truth. The relative ranking favoring strong_feed_reduction is more robust. There is residual uncertainty in hidden receiving parameters (OUR kinetics, Kla) — the strong feed cut may slow production rate somewhat, but model runs show no product-mass penalty vs alternatives, and mass is volume×concentration preserved. One extra assay was available but the online DO2 trace already gives decisive, timely evidence of the oxygen violation; a 4-h-turnaround assay would not change the intervention choice.
